doc.brief: Creates a custom titlebar for a window.
doc.md:
Creates a custom titlebar for a window.

`GtkHeaderBar` is similar to a horizontal `GtkCenterBox`. It allows
children to be placed at the start or the end. In addition, it allows
the window title to be displayed. The title will be centered with respect
to the width of the box, even if the children at either side take up
different amounts of space.

`GtkHeaderBar` can add typical window frame controls, such as minimize,
maximize and close buttons, or the window icon.

For these reasons, `GtkHeaderBar` is the natural choice for use as the
custom titlebar widget of a `GtkWindow` (see [`Window.set_titlebar()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Window#method:set_titlebar)),
as it gives features typical of titlebars while allowing the addition of
child widgets.

## GtkHeaderBar as GtkBuildable

The `GtkHeaderBar` implementation of the `GtkBuildable` interface supports
adding children at the start or end sides by specifying “start” or “end” as
the “type” attribute of a `<child>` element, or setting the title widget by
specifying “title” value.

By default the `GtkHeaderBar` uses a `GtkLabel` displaying the title of the
window it is contained in as the title widget, equivalent to the following
UI definition:

```xml
<object class="GtkHeaderBar">
  <property name="title-widget">
    <object class="GtkLabel">
      <property name="label" translatable="yes">Label</property>
      <property name="single-line-mode">True</property>
      <property name="ellipsize">end</property>
      <property name="width-chars">5</property>
      <style>
        <class name="title"/>
      </style>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

# CSS nodes

```
headerbar
╰── windowhandle
    ╰── box
        ├── box.start
        │   ├── windowcontrols.start
        │   ╰── [other children]
        ├── [Title Widget]
        ╰── box.end
            ├── [other children]
            ╰── windowcontrols.end
```

A `GtkHeaderBar`'s CSS node is called `headerbar`. It contains a `windowhandle`
subnode, which contains a `box` subnode, which contains two `box` subnodes at
the start and end of the header bar, as well as a center node that represents
the title.

Each of the boxes contains a `windowcontrols` subnode, see
[`WindowControls`](xref:gtk:Gtk.WindowControls) for details, as well as other children.

# Accessibility

`GtkHeaderBar` uses the [`AccessibleRole.group`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AccessibleRole#value:group) role.

remove.brief: Removes a child from the header bar.
remove.md:
Removes a child from the header bar.

The child must have been added with
[`HeaderBar.pack_start()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.HeaderBar#method:pack_start),
[`HeaderBar.pack_end()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.HeaderBar#method:pack_end) or
[`HeaderBar.set_title_widget()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.HeaderBar#method:set_title_widget).

set_decoration_layout.brief: Sets the decoration layout for this header bar.
set_decoration_layout.md:
Sets the decoration layout for this header bar.

This property overrides the
[`Settings:gtk-decoration-layout`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Settings#property:gtk-decoration-layout) setting.

There can be valid reasons for overriding the setting, such
as a header bar design that does not allow for buttons to take
room on the right, or only offers room for a single close button.
Split header bars are another example for overriding the setting.

The format of the string is button names, separated by commas.
A colon separates the buttons that should appear on the left
from those on the right. Recognized button names are minimize,
maximize, close and icon (the window icon).

For example, “icon:minimize,maximize,close” specifies an icon
on the left, and minimize, maximize and close buttons on the right.

set_show_title_buttons.brief: Sets whether this header bar shows the standard window title buttons.
set_show_title_buttons.md:
Sets whether this header bar shows the standard window
title buttons.

set_title_widget.brief: Sets the title for the header bar.
set_title_widget.md:
Sets the title for the header bar.

When set to `NULL`, the headerbar will display the title of
the window it is contained in.

The title should help a user identify the current view.
To achieve the same style as the builtin title, use the
“title” style class.

You should set the title widget to `NULL`, for the window
title label to be visible again.

set_use_native_controls.brief: Sets whether this header bar shows native window controls.
set_use_native_controls.md:
Sets whether this header bar shows native window controls.

This option shows the "stoplight" buttons on macOS.
For Linux, this option has no effect.

See also [Using GTK on Apple macOS](osx.html?native-window-controls).

decoration-layout.md:
The decoration layout for buttons.

If this property is not set, the
[`Settings:gtk-decoration-layout`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Settings#property:gtk-decoration-layout) setting is used.

show-title-buttons.brief: Whether to show title buttons like close, minimize, maximize.
show-title-buttons.md:
Whether to show title buttons like close, minimize, maximize.

Which buttons are actually shown and where is determined
by the [`HeaderBar:decoration-layout`](xref:gtk:Gtk.HeaderBar#property:decoration-layout) property,
and by the state of the window (e.g. a close button will not
be shown if the window can't be closed).

use-native-controls.brief: Whether to show platform native close/minimize/maximize buttons.
use-native-controls.md:
Whether to show platform native close/minimize/maximize buttons.

For macOS, the [`HeaderBar:decoration-layout`](xref:gtk:Gtk.HeaderBar#property:decoration-layout) property
can be used to enable/disable controls.

On Linux, this option has no effect.

See also [Using GTK on Apple macOS](osx.html?native-window-controls).
